title: Molecular basis and genetic testing strategies for diagnosing 21-hydroxylase deficiency, including CAH-X syndrome
supports: RCCX physical gene arrangement and CYP21A2–TNXB contiguous-gene disease; does not validate the proposed psychological cascade.

title: Schizophrenia risk from complex variation of complement component 4
supports: C4 structural alleles relate to schizophrenia risk and mouse postnatal pruning; phenotype and species boundaries apply.

title: Genome-wide analyses of ADHD identify 27 risk loci, refine the genetic architecture and implicate several cognitive domains
supports: ADHD has polygenic architecture; no one RCCX-centered etiology follows.

title: Epigenetic regulation of the glucocorticoid receptor in human brain associates with childhood abuse
supports: Abuse history was associated with hippocampal NR3C1 methylation and expression in a selected postmortem comparison.

title: The effects of childhood maltreatment on epigenetic regulation of stress-response associated genes: an intergenerational approach
supports: In 113 dyads, maternal associations appeared but direct transmission of assayed methylation sites to newborns was not found.

title: Intergenerational Effects of Maternal Holocaust Exposure on FKBP5 Methylation
supports: An FKBP5 site association replicated in 125 exposed offspring and 31 controls; transmission mechanism remains unresolved.

title: A meta-analytic study of event rate effects on Go/No-Go performance in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
supports: Task event rate moderates some ADHD performance differences; general group differences persist.

title: Attention deficits linked with proclivity to explore while foraging
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
supports: Among 457 participants, positive ADHD screen was associated with earlier patch departure; no ancestral subtype or universal advantage was established.

title: Chronotype variation drives night-time sentinel-like behaviour in hunter-gatherers
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
supports: One or more group members were scored awake or in light sleep in 99.8% of sampled epochs across 20 days; no ADHD mechanism was tested.

title: Gabapentin receptor α2δ-1 is a neuronal thrombospondin receptor responsible for excitatory CNS synaptogenesis
supports: α2δ-1 participates in thrombospondin-induced new excitatory synapse formation; this is distinct from channel trafficking.

title: Nerve injury increases native CaV2.2 trafficking in dorsal root ganglion mechanoreceptors
supports: α2δ-1 was required for increased CaV2.2 surface and terminal localization after nerve injury; not a perinatal brain result.

title: Voltage-activated calcium channel expression profiles in mouse brain and cultured hippocampal neurons
supports: Calcium-channel subunit expression differs by brain region and developmental stage; activity blockade did not alter the measured expression program.

title: Direct, gabapentin-insensitive interaction of a soluble form of the calcium channel subunit α2δ-1 with thrombospondin-4
supports: Gabapentin did not directly block measured TSP4–α2δ-1 binding; challenges a simple drug-blocks-ligand story.

title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
supports: AI story ideas improved rated individual short stories while increasing similarity across stories; outside-task generalization is open.

title: Development and Validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q)
venue: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
supports: Autistic camouflaging is measurable in adult samples; does not prove a universal subconscious masking mechanism.

title: A new insight on postural tachycardia syndrome in 102 adults with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome/hypermobility spectrum disorder
supports: Autonomic profiles were heterogeneous; POTS occurred in 48% of this selected cohort, not the general population.

title: Methylation of the FKBP5 gene in association with FKBP5 genotypes, childhood maltreatment and depression
supports: In 3,965 adults, previously reported childhood maltreatment interactions at assayed FKBP5 sites were not replicated.

title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental epileptic encephalopathy
supports: Severe biallelic CACNA2D1 loss impaired CaV2 trafficking and was linked to early epileptic encephalopathy; not evidence for common trait variation.
